Through this work, we aim to generate well-characterised quantitative datasets and link automated experiments with physical models, enabling closed-loop workflows in which measurements inform models and model predictions guide subsequent experiments. Integrating laboratory instruments and robotic systems for reliable operation across experimental procedures. Developing, testing, and maintaining software for instrument control, experimental processes, and data processing, using version control and well-documented code. Validating and benchmarking new methods with biological controls, assessing sample quality, reproducibility, throughput, and robustness. Maintaining and improving established systems through troubleshooting, calibration, cleaning, servicing, and recovery after interruptions. Documenting protocols, equipment configurations, and experimental data, including metadata and execution logs, and training colleagues to use validated methods. Strong practical understanding of biological experiments and experience developing, adapting, or validating laboratory protocols. Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, with the ability to develop reliable and maintainable scientific software. Experience planning and implementing scientific or technical development projects, including systematic testing and troubleshooting. Excellent English communication skills and the ability to collaborate across disciplines. Experience with liquid-handling platforms, laboratory robotics, instrument integration, or automated experimental workflows is advantageous. Familiarity with experimental data and metadata systems would be advantageous, as would an interest in physical modelling, AI-assisted experimental design, or closed-loop experimentation. Our offer: An opportunity to help establish a new scientific facility at the interface of experimental biology, robotics, and software engineering. A full-time position with an initial two-year contract and the possibility of an extension for up to three additional years. Salary and benefits in accordance with the German public-sector collective agreement (TVöD Bund), up to EG13. Public-sector benefits including 31 days of annual leave, full social coverage, and supplementary pension (VBL). A discounted public-transport job ticket (VVO) and excellent transport connections. Support for work-life balance, including assistance with family and childcare matters. A broad network for career development and training through the Max Planck Society.
